finding: P24 is scored 'between' but its registered refutation clause is met. The clause is 'at or below 1.7 percent (the row bootstrap value)'. The exact round 4 row bootstrap upper bound is 1.72035, and the cluster upper bound is the same 1.72035, so the cluster bound is at (not above) the row bootstrap value. The script compares against the rounded literal 1.7, which is the reading more favourable to the prediction. That breaks the rule stated in the scores header (use the less favourable reading and name it).

The less favourable reading rule is not applied the same way everywhere. P6 (flights processed; refuted if fewer than 20) and P9 (completed missions per configuration; refuted if fewer than 10) are count metrics that can be computed, and both counts are 0. Read literally, both refutation clauses are met. The script marks them 'not scored' (tool or source unavailable) without naming the second reading, while P19, P21, P22 and P26 are pushed to the stricter reading.
note: P6 scored miss; P9 scored from the runs

finding: The P21 miss rests on firmware_counter_unsigned_version. That model variant is weaker than the design and was not in the registered clause. The stated firmware design already signs the image and its version (FORMAL_VERIFICATION F3: 'Stated design (signature over image and version, no counter)'), so 'the stated design plus a counter' is firmware_fixed_counter, which is proved, while the no counter model gives a counterexample. That is exactly the registered prediction. The score treats an added variant as a reading of the clause and does not name the alternative reading (hit).

P35 is scored 'hit' by a string test ("LMS" in the text and "session" in the lowercased text) that cannot fail in practice, so the verdict is not computed from any rerun. The registered refutation is that either design changes. In this round the command design did change (a vehicle ML-DSA-44 signature, a fourth flight and key confirmation, F1), and so did the firmware design (signed version plus monotonic counter, F3). The evidence text even says 'now with the vehicle signature'. Under the less favourable reading this is a miss or between, and the reading is not named.
note: P35 scored miss under the stricter reading

finding: P25 is scored 'between' (compiler largest) from the main unweighted fit only. In that fit the compiler share (50.1 percent) and the statistic share (39.4 percent) have the same interval, 0.0 to 87.4 percent, so the largest factor is not identified. Also, the 'statistic' factor is a regular expression classifier in which 'other' (87 rows) mixes 'not stated' with worst case, and compiler 'not stated' is one level holding 204 of 408 rows.
